settings.text:
You already know what he looks like. Charming. Intense. The kind of man who makes your heart race from the first conversation. The kind who texts you at midnight but disappears by morning. The kind who makes you feel chosen — until he makes you feel invisible.

And every time it ends the same way. The ghosting. The slow fade. The excuses that stopped making sense three situationships ago.

Your friends tell you to trust your gut. But your gut has been wrong every time. Because this is not a gut problem. It is a pattern. And patterns do not break themselves.

settings.heading: What you are calling chemistry is your nervous system recognizing a familiar pattern of pain.

settings.text:
Attachment theory — one of the most researched frameworks in psychology — explains why you keep choosing the same kind of person. The bonds we formed with caregivers in early childhood create internal models of what love feels like. For people with insecure attachment styles, the feelings they associate with love — intensity, anxiety, obsession — are actually their attachment system in distress.

What you have been calling chemistry might be a trauma bond. It uses the same brain chemicals as genuine connection. That is why leaving feels impossible and going back feels like relief.

This is not a character flaw. It is a pattern encoded in your nervous system. And the science tells us exactly how to break it.

This is what the 30-Day POV Never Get Played Again Journal was built to do.

settings.title: Attachment Theory
settings.text: Developed by John Bowlby and extended by decades of peer-reviewed research — helps you identify your attachment style, understand how it formed, and recognize how it has been driving every romantic choice you have made. This is not about blaming your past. It is about understanding the invisible pattern so you can finally change it.

settings.title: Boundary Psychology
settings.text: Drawn from the work of Nedra Tawwab, Henry Cloud, and the broader field of relational psychology — gives you the tools to establish and hold limits that reflect your actual values. Red flag recognition systems. Non-negotiables. The ability to say no without guilt.

settings.title: Built on attachment theory and boundary psychology. Not dating advice.

settings.heading: 30 days. Four weeks. A pattern broken for good.

settings.text:
This is a structured 30-day system. One prompt per day, sequenced intentionally. Week 1 identifies the pattern and its roots. Week 2 maps your attachment style and explains why chaos felt like love. Week 3 builds a red flag recognition system. Week 4 creates your personal Love Manifesto — new relationship criteria built on what you actually deserve, not what your nervous system has been trained to accept.

10 to 20 minutes per day. No dating advice. No "just trust yourself." A system that works at the root.

When you open your POV Never Get Played Again Journal, you will find a contract. You sign it. You name an accountability partner — someone who knows you are doing this work and will check in with you.

Because breaking a pattern is harder than recognizing one. And having someone witness your commitment makes it real.
